```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(flextable)

res <- readRDS(
  here::here(
    "02_data_output",
    "dig_req_llm_metadata_2.rds"
  )
)

flat <- res |>
  mutate(
    summary = map_chr(
      metadata_v3,
      ~ .x$summary %||% NA_character_
    ),
    business_area = map_chr(
      metadata_v3,
      ~ .x$business_area %||% NA_character_
    ),
    themes = map(
      metadata_v3,
      ~ unlist(.x$themes)
    )
  )

themes <- flat |>
  select(
    request_row_id,
    digital_request_number,
    business_area,
    themes
  ) |>
  unnest(themes) |>
  distinct(digital_request_number, themes, .keep_all = TRUE)

theme_counts <- themes |>
  count(themes, sort = TRUE) |>
  filter(n >= 2)

top_theme <- theme_counts |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 1) |>
  dplyr::pull(themes)

# create flat metadata table for later use in report
flat_metadata <- res |>
  select(
    request_row_id,
    digital_request_number,
    source_record,
    metadata_v3
  ) |>
  unnest_wider(
    source_record,
    names_sep = "_"
  ) |>
  unnest_wider(metadata_v3)

# Flextable ---------------

theme_ft <- function(x) {
  x |>
  autofit() |>
  theme_booktabs()
  }

# DT:datatable ------------------------------------------------------------

# Use DT:datatable to embed an interactive table with export options in an R session or markdown document

# copied from github: jbisanz/qiime2R/R/interactive_table.R
# https://rstudio.github.io/DT/options.html ... "DataTables has a large number of initialization options, which make it very flexible to customize the table."

interactive_table <- function(table, 
                              nrow = 5, 
                              not_as_factor = c("mrn", 
                                                "patient"
                                                ),
                              autoWidth = TRUE
) {
  # mutate(across(where(is.character) using forcats::as_factor, avoiding items in "not_as_factor"
  table <- table |> 
    mutate(across(where(is.character) 
                  & !matches(not_as_factor), 
                  forcats::as_factor))
  
  # configure table settings
  dtable <- DT::datatable(table, 
                          extensions = 'Buttons', 
                          filter = "top",
                          options = list(
                            pageLength = nrow, #nrow dictates pageLength,
                            #lengthMenu = c(5, 10, 15, 20),
                            # initComplete = JS(
                            #   "function(settings, json) {",
                            #   "$(this.api().table().header()).css({'background-color': '#000', 'color': '#fff'});", #we use the initComplete callback function in options to change the background color of the table header to black after the initialization:
                            #   "}"
                            dom = 'Bfrtip', 
                            buttons = c('copy',
                                        'csv',
                                        #'pdf',
                                        'excel'
                                        ),
                            autoWidth = autoWidth,
                            searchHighlight = TRUE)
  )
  
  return(dtable)
}


```

# Executive summary

`r nrow(flat_metadata)` requests were analysed across
`r n_distinct(flat_metadata$business_area)` business areas.

The most common theme was **`r top_theme`**.

The sections below summarise request themes, business areas, complexity indicators and opportunities to identify related requests.

# Overview

This report summarises themes identified from digital requests using locally-hosted LLM-generated metadata.

The report is intended to support prioritisation and portfolio review by:

* identifying common request themes
* highlighting potentially related or duplicate requests
* summarising requests by business area

## Summary statistics

```{r}
summary_tbl <- tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "Requests analysed",
    "Business areas",
    "Themes"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(flat),
    n_distinct(flat$business_area, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_distinct(themes$themes, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

summary_tbl |>
  flextable() |>
  theme_ft()
```

# Most common themes

## Top 20 themes

```{r}
theme_counts |>
  slice_head(n = 20) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = reorder(themes, n),
      y = n
    )
  ) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = "Themes",
    y = "Requests (n)"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = n),
    hjust = -0.2
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Word cloud

```{r}
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 12

theme_counts |>
  slice_head(n = 75) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      label = themes,
      size = n,
      colour = n
    )
  ) +
  ggwordcloud::geom_text_wordcloud_area(
    eccentricity = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_size_area(
    max_size = 60
  ) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c() +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  )
```




# Request summaries

A concise, board-friendly overview, to answer the question `What requests do we have?`

```{r}
flat_metadata |>
  transmute(
    `Request` = digital_request_number,
    `Business area` = business_area,
    Themes = map_chr(themes, paste, collapse = "; "),
    Summary = summary
  ) |>
  arrange(
    `Business area`,
    `Request`
  ) |>
  interactive_table(
    nrow = 5,
    not_as_factor = c(
      "Themes",
      "Summary"
    )
  )
```

## Detailed request metadata

A fuller view for identifying overlaps, dependencies, risks and opportunities to consolidate work, to answer the question `What exactly are they asking for?`

```{r}
flat_metadata |>
  transmute(
    Request = paste0(
      digital_request_number,
      " - ",
      source_record_project_title
    ),
    `Business area` = business_area,
    `Key problem` = key_problem,
    `Requested outcome` = requested_outcome,
    `Expected benefits` = map_chr(
      expected_benefits,
      paste,
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    Themes = map_chr(themes, paste, collapse = "; "),
    Stakeholders = map_chr(stakeholders, paste, collapse = "; "),
    Dependencies = map_chr(dependencies, paste, collapse = "; "),
    #`Dependencies (n)` = lengths(dependencies),
    `Risks and constraints` = map_chr(
      risks_or_constraints,
      paste,
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    `Complexity score` =
  lengths(themes) +
  lengths(stakeholders) +
  2 * lengths(dependencies) +
  2 * lengths(risks_or_constraints)
    #`Risks (n)` = lengths(risks_or_constraints)
  ) |>
  arrange(
    #desc(`Dependencies (n)`),
    #desc(`Risks (n)`),
    desc(`Complexity score`),
    `Request`
  ) |>
  interactive_table(
    nrow = 5,
    not_as_factor = c(
      "Themes",
      "Key problem",
      "Requested outcome",
      "Stakeholders",
      "Dependencies",
      "Risks and constraints",
      "Expected benefits"
    )
  )
```

## Requests with the highest complexity

Compact portfolio-management table, to answer the question `Which requests look biggest or most interconnected?`

```{r}
flat_metadata |>
  transmute(
    Request = paste0(
      digital_request_number,
      " - ",
      source_record_project_title
    ),
    `Business area` = business_area,
    `Themes (n)` = lengths(themes),
    `Stakeholders (n)` = lengths(stakeholders),
    `Dependencies (n)` = lengths(dependencies),
    `Risks (n)` = lengths(risks_or_constraints),
    `Complexity score` =
      lengths(themes) +
      lengths(stakeholders) +
      2 * lengths(dependencies) +
      2 * lengths(risks_or_constraints)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(`Complexity score`)) |>
  interactive_table(
    nrow = 10,
    not_as_factor = "Request"
  )
```

# Appendix

## Heatmap: Themes x Business area

```{r}
theme_business <- themes |>
  count(
    business_area,
    themes
  ) |>
  mutate(
    business_area = forcats::fct_reorder(
      business_area,
      n,
      .fun = sum
    ),
    themes = forcats::fct_reorder(
      themes,
      n,
      .fun = sum
    )
  )

ggplot(
  theme_business,
  aes(
    x = themes,
    y = business_area,
    fill = n
  )
) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Themes",
    y = "Business area",
    fill = "Requests (n)"
  )
```

## Business area frequencies

```{r}
flat_metadata |>
  count(
    business_area,
    sort = TRUE
  ) |>
  rename(
    Requests = n
  ) |>
  flextable() |>
  theme_ft()
```

## Potentially related requests

Requests that share multiple themes may represent:

* similar problems
* opportunities for collaboration
* duplicate requests
* opportunities to consolidate work

```{r}
pairs <- inner_join(
  themes,
  themes,
  by = "themes",
  relationship = "many-to-many"
) |>
  filter(
    digital_request_number.x < digital_request_number.y
  ) |>
  group_by(
    digital_request_number.x,
    digital_request_number.y
  ) |>
  summarise(
    shared_themes = paste(
      sort(unique(themes)),
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    n_shared_themes = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n_shared_themes >= 2) |>
  arrange(
    desc(n_shared_themes),
    digital_request_number.x,
    digital_request_number.y
  )

pairs |>
    interactive_table(nrow = 5,
                                      not_as_factor = c("mrn",
                                                        "patient"
                                                        ),
                                )
```
